extracted.intended_audience: Prospective applicants to the Fulbright U.S. Student Program (U.S. enrolled students, non-enrolled U.S. applicants, artists) and prospective international applicants seeking U.S. awards
extracted.subtask_description: Official 'Getting Started' guidance for prospective applicants to the Fulbright U.S. Student Program describing who is eligible, how/where to apply, award types, and next steps (e.g., finding a campus Fulbright Program Adviser).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — Current U.S. Students
rubrics_metrics.description: United States citizens who are currently enrolled in undergraduate or graduate degree programs are eligible to apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you are currently enrolled in an undergraduate or graduate program at a U.S. college or university, you will apply through that institution, even if you are not currently a resident there. Find the Fulbright Program Adviser on your campus for assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — Non-enrolled U.S. Citizens (degree-holders)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are a U.S. citizen, will hold a bachelor’s degree by the award start date, and do not have a Ph.D. degree, then you are eligible to apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-enrolled applicants should have relatively limited professional experience in the fields in which they are applying (typically 7 years or less). Candidates with more experience should consider applying for the Fulbright Scholar Program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional Experience Expectation (typical 7 years)
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-enrolled applicants and arts candidates should have relatively limited professional experience (typically 7 years or less) in the fields in which they are applying.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants with substantially more professional experience are directed to consider the Fulbright Scholar Program instead of the U.S. Student Program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility & Guidance for Artists / Creative & Performing Arts
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fulbright U.S. Student Program welcomes applications in the creative and performing arts; arts candidates should have relatively limited professional experience (typically 7 years or less).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creative & Performing Arts projects fall under the Study/Research grant category and are available in all countries where Study/Research grants are offered. Artists with more experience should consider the Fulbright Scholar Program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Channel — Campus Fulbright Program Adviser (FPA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prospective applicants are advised to Find the Fulbright Program Adviser on your campus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Connect with a Fulbright Program Adviser for guidance on preparing and submitting applications; campus FPAs support students in applying for U.S. Student Program awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Channel — Professors/Administrators (Fulbright Scholar)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are a U.S. citizen and a professor or administrator at a U.S. institution and are interested in applying for a Fulbright Scholar Award, you will need to apply through fulbrightscholars.org.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Faculty/administrators should use the Fulbright Scholar program site rather than the U.S. Student application route; FPAs can help students but faculty use the separate scholar application process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-U.S. Citizens Applying to the United States — Local Commission/Embassy
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are a non-U.S. citizen interested in applying for a Fulbright Award to the United States, you will need to apply through the Fulbright Commission or U.S. Embassy in your home country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to Fulbright Visiting Scholar Program or Fulbright Foreign Student Program for more information and country-specific procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Purpose — Permitted Activities (U.S. Student Program)
rubrics_metrics.description: The U.S. Student Program funds American citizens to study, conduct research, or teach English abroad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Award opportunities are open in all academic disciplines, including the creative and performing arts; choose the appropriate award type (Study/Research, English Teaching Assistant, etc.) based on intended activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award Types & Specialized Programs
rubrics_metrics.description: U.S. Student award categories include Study/Research Awards, English Teaching Assistant Awards (ETA), Fulbright-National Geographic Award Program, Fulbright-Fogarty Fellowships in Public Health, and others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some specialized awards (e.g., Creative & Performing Arts projects) are categorized under Study/Research; consult the award-specific pages for component requirements and country availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Timing and National Deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Application cycles have specific open/closed status and national deadlines; for example, the 2027–2028 Award Cycle application is now open and the National Deadline is Tuesday, October 6, 2026 at 5 pm Eastern Time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the current competition year for whether application is open or closed and note that final notifications may be on a rolling basis through the spring. Missing national deadlines can disqualify an application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resources & Support — Webinars and Application Components
rubrics_metrics.description: The program provides webinars (e.g., 'Application Tips: Statement of Grant Purpose'), tutorials, and pages describing application components (Study/Research: Academic; Study/Research: Creative & Performing Arts; ETA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attend webinars, review application component guidance, and use resources (ASPE Assist 24/7 Support, Fulbright Program Adviser) to prepare application materials correctly.
